content: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) campus is situated in Bethesda, Maryland. This campus serves as the primary location for the Divisions of Intramural Research for most of the NIH institutes, with these divisions distributed across various buildings on the premises. The campus is geographically bordered by Old Georgetown Road to the west, Wisconsin Avenue to the east, West Cedar Lane to the north, and downtown Bethesda to the south. Directly across Wisconsin Avenue from the campus lies the National Naval Medical Center. Additionally, the campus is located just a few miles north of the Washington, D.C. border. For public transportation access, the Medical Center Metro station is conveniently located just outside the campus fence along Wisconsin Avenue. The NIH Bethesda campus has been in use since 1938, marking its expansion beyond Washington, D.C., where the original National Institute of Health was based. In 1953, the Clinical Center, also known as Building 10, was inaugurated with a capacity of 540 beds, enabling the conduct of clinical research. The establishment of research protocols at this facility was heavily influenced by the ethical considerations that arose in response to the inhumane medical experiments conducted during World War II. As a result, all research protocols underwent ethical review by a designated review board. The campus comprises more than fifty buildings, each assigned a number corresponding to the order in which they were constructed. Immediate access to the campus requires a Department of Health and Human Services identification card. Visitors must present a government-issued photo ID to obtain a pass, and both individuals and vehicles are subject to inspection as part of the security protocols.
